purpose: Replace rectangular and computational proxy ROIs with genuinely independent human anatomical annotations before any confirmatory claim about multilayer Wedjat morphology.

source_basis.MET_547767: Museum description explicitly separates a human eye, horizontal cosmetic line, vertical falcon marking, and diagonal falcon line ending in a spiral.
source_basis.MET_551474: Museum description independently notes that the New Kingdom spiral sits directly under the cosmetic line and is lower in later examples.
source_basis.MET_555588: Museum description identifies Wedjat as a combination of human and falcon eye morphology.

blind_packet.independence: Annotators work separately and cannot view each other's masks, landmarks, notes, or confidence scores until both submissions are SHA-256 frozen.
hidden_from_annotators: expected direction of the spiral chronology test
blind_packet.image_processing_before_annotation: No crop, mirror, rotation, contrast tuning, denoise, or rescale except lossless UI display scaling. Original source dimensions and orientation remain authoritative.
blind_packet.unlock_rule: Glyph matching, chronology metadata, and fraction labels stay inaccessible until both annotation packages are committed and hashed.

components.representation: polyline plus optional narrow polygon mask
components.definition: Visible eyebrow/upper-eye element running above or along the upper eye. Do not include suspension loops or external ornamental frame elements.
Human-eye-shaped principal eye contour, excluding the pupil/iris and excluding lower falcon facial markings.
Central pupil/iris marking if visibly distinct. Do not infer a pupil from symmetry when no marking is visible.
Predominantly vertical falcon-derived marking below the pupil/eye region. Do not merge with the diagonal mark merely because the two touch.
Diagonal lower facial marking extending away from the eye toward the curl/spiral region, excluding the spiral itself after the tangent transition.

Curl/spiral terminal of the diagonal falcon marking. Begin at the first clear tangent-to-curvature transition and end at the visible terminal. If no spiral is separable, mark NOT_SEPARABLE rather than guessing.

coordinate_rule: Store integer pixel coordinates in the exact original source image coordinate system; normalized coordinates may be derived later but never replace raw pixels.

agreement_gates.visibility_state_rule: VISIBLE/PARTIAL agreement is required for primary scoring. Any ABSENT/NOT_SEPARABLE disagreement triggers adjudication.
agreement_gates.failure_action: A third independent annotator receives the same blind packet. Use median geometry only if the anatomical definition remains unchanged; otherwise mark ANATOMICAL_DISAGREEMENT and exclude that component/object from the primary test.

post_freeze_scoring.glyph_inventory: full Egyptian Hieroglyphs Unicode block as a modern morphology reference only
tests: For each anatomical component and annotator-consensus mask, rank all glyphs with one frozen similarity metric.
Test whether A1/A2 show cross-object enrichment of the predeclared eye family relative to all glyphs and a same-D-class control.
Treat D012-pupil and D013-eyebrow correspondences as modern annotation sanity checks, not proof of ancient fraction derivation.
Discover lower-mark candidate glyph families only on a training subset, freeze them, then evaluate a held-out period group.
Run leave-one-period-group-out summaries without retuning masks or thresholds.

promotion_rules.UPPER_EYE_LAYER_REPLICATED: Both independent annotators pass agreement and at least three period groups independently show eye-family enrichment in A1/A2 under the frozen scoring rule.
promotion_rules.LOWER_FALCON_LAYER_CANDIDATE: A4/A5/A6 pass agreement and a frozen lower-family signature discovered on training objects replicates in a held-out period group.
promotion_rules.MULTILAYER_WEDJAT_GRAMMAR_CANDIDATE: Upper-eye and lower-falcon layers both replicate under independent annotation and period holdout, with materially different glyph-family profiles.

next_gate: Acquire/freeze the full eligible museum-image corpus, generate anonymized annotation packets, collect two genuinely independent human submissions, SHA-256 freeze them, and only then unlock glyph scoring.
